answer.evidence: The plinth is a flat front elevation. Its cap at rows 15-16 is only a 2-row lip (light row 15, slightly darker row 16, a 1-row shadow at row 17 on the right). That is a rim, not a top surface seen from above. Below it are a flat shaft (rows 17-26, width 12) and a base flange (rows 27-31, width 14) with no top plane of their own. The display case and figurine in rows 0-14 are decor on top of the plinth. No ellipse, no visible contents, and no band of 3+ rows with a front-edge line.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stone plinth with a bust or figure on top. It measures 22 visible tones per full tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it is at or above the references on the main density fact. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills; the stone shows stepped light-to-dark faces and the top figure has its own accent tones. Only 22% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, which means the outline leans toward the tint of the neighbouring stone and is not a uniform black sticker line. It is slightly shallower than the best references, at roughly 5 stone steps against 5-6, and it is small and simple. Even so, it would sit next to the well and stall without looking thinner or flatter.
